input.question: Helicopter tail rotors? Why are they so important?
input.ground_truth: The torque required for the main rotor has an opposite torque acting on the rest of the frame. That is, if the main rotor is spinning clockwise, the rest of the frame is being torqued counterclockwise. The tail rotor acts to counteract the torque and keep the frame pointing in the right direction.

Question: Helicopter tail rotors? Why are they so important?

Okay! Imagine a helicopter is like a big flying toy with a long tail. That long tail has a special spinning part called a "tail rotor."

Now, when the helicopter’s big propeller on top spins to make the helicopter go up, it wants to make the whole helicopter spin around the other way, like when you spin around really fast and then stop and feel dizzy.

The tail rotor is like a little helper. Its job is to spin the other way and push the helicopter’s tail so it doesn’t spin around and fall over. That way, the helicopter can fly straight and not get all wobbly!

So, the tail rotor is super important because it helps the helicopter fly straight and not spin out of control.
